title: Big Stone
simplified_paragraphs: 从前，一户人家的门前有一块大石头。这块石头不但妨碍大家进出，而且还常常有人被它绊倒。
有一天，这户人家的儿子问他父亲：”爸爸，门前的那块石头那么危险，我们一起来把它搬走吧！”父亲笑着回答：”那块大石头很重的，我爷爷生活的时代，那块石头就在了。如果那么简单就能搬走，哪会让它留到现在啊？”
不过，儿子没有放弃。第二天，他自己用锄头把大石头周围的泥土都挖开，没想到很快整个大石头就松动了。他赶快叫别人来帮忙，轻而易举地就把那块石头搬走了。
有时阻碍我们去发现、去创造的，正是我们自己一直”认为”的东西。没有真正尝试过，怎么知道事情一定会像我们想的一样呢？
traditional_paragraphs: 從前，一戶人家的門前有一塊大石頭。這塊石頭不但妨礙大家進出，而且還常常有人被它絆倒。
有一天，這戶人家的兒子問他父親：”爸爸，門前的那塊石頭那麼危險，我們一起來把它搬走吧！”父親笑著回答：”那塊大石頭很重的，我爺爺生活的時代，那塊石頭就在了。如果那麼簡單就能搬走，哪會讓它留到現在啊？”
不過，兒子沒有放棄。第二天，他自己用鋤頭把大石頭周圍的泥土都挖開，沒想到很快整個大石頭就鬆動了。他趕快叫別人來幫忙，輕而易舉地就把那塊石頭搬走了。
有時阻礙我們去發現、去創造的，正是我們自己一直”認為”的東西。沒有真正嘗試過，怎麼知道事情一定會像我們想的一樣呢？
pinyin_paragraphs: cóng qián， yī hù rén jiā de mén qián yǒu yī kuài dà shí tou。 zhè kuài shí tou bù dàn fáng ài dà jiā jìn chū， ér qiě hái cháng cháng yǒu rén bèi tā bàn dǎo。

yǒu yì tiān， zhè hù rén jiā de ér zi wèn tā fù qīn：” bà ba， mén qián de nà kuài shí tou nà me wēi xiǎn， wǒ men yī qǐ lái bǎ tā bān zǒu ba！” fù qīn xiào zhe huí dá：” nà kuài dà shí tou hěn zhòng de， wǒ yé ye shēng huó de shí dài， nà kuài shí tou jiù zài le。 rú guǒ nà me jiǎn dān jiù néng bān zǒu， nǎ huì ràng tā liú dào xiàn zài a？”

bù guò， ér zi méi yǒu fàng qì。 dì èr tiān， tā zì jǐ yòng chú tou bǎ dà shí tou zhōu wéi de ní tǔ dōu wā kāi， méi xiǎng dào hěn kuài zhěng gè dà shí tou jiù sōng dòng le。 tā gǎn kuài jiào bié rén lái bāng máng， qīng ér yì jǔ de jiù bǎ nà kuài shí tou bān zǒu le。

yǒu shí zǔ ài wǒ men qù fā xiàn、 qù chuàng zào de， zhèng shì wǒ men zì jǐ yī zhí” rèn wéi” de dōng xi。 méi yǒu zhēn zhèng cháng shì guo， zěn me zhī dào shì qing yī dìng huì xiàng wǒ men xiǎng de yī yàng ne？
english_paragraphs: Once upon a time, there was a large stone in front of a family’s house. It got in everyone’s way as they came and went, and people often tripped over it.

One day, the family’s son asked his father, “Dad, that stone in front of the house is dangerous. Let’s move it together!” His father smiled and replied, “That stone is very heavy. It was already there when my grandfather was alive. If it were that easy to move, do you think it would still be there now?”

But the son did not give up. The next day, he used a hoe to dig away the soil around the stone. To his surprise, the whole stone soon came loose. He quickly called some people to help, and they moved it with ease.

Sometimes, what stops us from discovering and creating new things is what we have always assumed to be true. If we have never really tried, how can we know for sure that things will turn out the way we expect?
english_full:
Once upon a time, there was a large stone in front of a family’s house. It got in everyone’s way as they came and went, and people often tripped over it.

One day, the family’s son asked his father, “Dad, that stone in front of the house is dangerous. Let’s move it together!” His father smiled and replied, “That stone is very heavy. It was already there when my grandfather was alive. If it were that easy to move, do you think it would still be there now?”

But the son did not give up. The next day, he used a hoe to dig away the soil around the stone. To his surprise, the whole stone soon came loose. He quickly called some people to help, and they moved it with ease.

Sometimes, what stops us from discovering and creating new things is what we have always assumed to be true. If we have never really tried, how can we know for sure that things will turn out the way we expect?
